e2el.d: Time from sending the request to the last token: \(t_N - t_0\) = TTFT + decode window. Dividing tokens by E2EL mixes prefill and decode into a number that describes neither.

escada-de-concorrencia.d: The same load repeated with 1, 2, 4, 8… simultaneous streams, recording at each rung the aggregate, per-stream rate, TTFT (p50/p95), preemptions and cache hit rate. It shows the knee and the point where queueing starts.

joelho.d: The rung of the ladder beyond which more streams stop increasing the aggregate in the same proportion: the marginal cost per sequence (\(\delta B\)) starts to weigh on the step, or the engine runs out of slots/KV.

prefill-frio.d: Prefill measured with no block coming from the prefix cache: a unique nonce at the start of the prompt (or a cache reset) and confirmation via cached_tokens = 0 or Δhits = 0. “Cold” as in cache, but with the kernels already warmed up.

prometheus-metrics.d: vLLM's text endpoint in the name{labels} value format: _total counters that only go up since boot, gauges and histograms. It sums the traffic of all clients, which is why it is read by delta.

medicao-por-delta.d: Reading the cumulative counters before and after the workload and using only the difference (e.g. Δaccepted/Δdrafts). It isolates your experiment from the server's history; a negative delta gives away a restart.

histograma-prometheus.d: A metric published as three series: _bucket{le=…} (cumulative counts per bucket), _sum (sum of the values) and _count. The mean over a window is Δsum/Δcount, like the ms/step of sweep.py.

percentil.d: The value below which a given fraction of the measurements falls: p50 is the median, p95 leaves out the worst 5%. For latency, the tail (p95/p99) is what the user feels at the worst moments.

faixa-de-ruido.d: The spread (min–max or standard deviation) of the baseline under identical conditions. A knob only wins if its trials land outside this band; in DeepSeek, c=1 varies ±10 tok/s and TTFT ±2%.

ab-a.d: Experimental design: baseline, change and baseline again, with repetitions and a median per arm. The effect is \(\tilde B / \text{mean}(\tilde A_1, \tilde A_2) - 1\) and \(\tilde A_2/\tilde A_1 - 1\) measures the drift of the session.

deriva.d: Slow change in the system over the session (page cache, swap, other processes, temperature) that shifts every number. In a naive A/B it becomes a false effect; A/B/A measures it.

bootstrap-ic.d: A confidence interval obtained by resampling the trials with replacement thousands of times and recomputing the effect. Paired when each B trial is compared with its A partner. If it doesn't cross zero, the effect is distinguishable from noise.

gate-de-memoria.d: A rule that forbids measuring (or rejects a knob) if the host's free memory drops too far. In DeepSeek's A/B: MemAvailable ≥ 3 GB on both nodes (AB_MEM_GATE_KB) and rejection of any knob that costs ≥ 0.5 GB or increases swap.

teste-de-fumaca.d: A quick, cheap check that the service responds sensibly (e.g. 6 “Reply with OK” requests at temperature 0, one per slot). It doesn't measure performance; it decides whether measuring is worth it.

best-seen.d: A number from a good day, used as a ceiling and not as an expectation. The DeepSeek audit (C1 73–76 tok/s) is treated this way because ordinary days on the same lane measured 52–57.

torch-profiler.d: PyTorch's profiler, which records CPU and GPU operators and kernels in a trace. In vLLM it is turned on via --profiler-config or VLLM_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR + /start_profile//stop_profile; it captures few iterations because of its cost.

efeito-observador.d: Distortion caused by the measurement itself. DSpark's stage timers record CUDA events and call synchronize() at the end of each stage: the CPU sits idle until the GPU finishes and doesn't enqueue the next piece of work, so CPU/GPU overlap and async scheduling are lost and the measured engine is slower than the real one. That's why these timers stay out of benchmarks.

py-spy.d: A Python stack sampler that attaches to a live (or hung) process without restarting it; py-spy dump shows where each thread is. In a container it needs --cap-add SYS_PTRACE.

vllm-bench-serve.d: vLLM's load generator against an OpenAI-compatible server: datasets (random, custom…), max concurrency, seed and percentiles of TTFT, TPOT, ITL and E2EL. The random dataset tanks speculative acceptance.

sparkdash.d: Mia's AI Lab benchmark dashboard for the DGX Spark: decode with 1 to N simultaneous streams (prose, structured, code, JSON) and cold prefill, run through the OpenAI API from another machine, under the lab protocol (temperature 0, thinking off). It is the single source of the numbers of GLM's TensorFold lane and also measured ladders of the vLLM recipe.

clocks-travados.d: Pinning the GPU frequency (minimum = maximum) or just capping it, to take boost variation between runs and between ranks out of the number. GLM's TensorFold lane measures with the clocks capped at 2,200 MHz: the cap cuts off boost and its oscillation, but does not prevent throttling below it. At TP=2 the slowest rank sets the pace of each round, so the effect is larger. On the GB10, which has no application clocks, the lever is nvidia-smi -lgc MIN,MAX.

gate-de-exatidao.d: A binary check that goes with every performance number on an exact engine: the reply with drafts must be identical to the serial one ("draft": false) and the one served alongside other requests, identical to the one served alone (reference hashes). A knob declared “same bits” that changes the hash is a bug, not a gain.

ruido-de-conteudo.d: Two sources of variation between trials of the same prompt. Content: which tokens come out, hence how many drafts are accepted and how many rounds the reply takes (it nearly vanishes with greedy and vanishes with keyed sampling, as long as the prompt is identical). Timing: how much each round costs (clock, network, host; it shrinks with a clock cap).

brier-score.d: Mean squared error between predicted probabilities and 0/1 outcomes: \( \frac{1}{n}\sum (q - y)^2 \). Together with log loss and AUC, it is one of the metrics TensorFold's draft simulator uses to score acceptance predictors.
